sentences.text:
Petitioner :- Suprabhat Banerji
Respondent :- State Of U.P. Thru Prin.Secy. Technical Education And Anr.

Counsel for Petitioner :- Abdul Haleem,Mohd. Shameem Khan,Ranjit Yadav,Uttam Kumar Verma
Counsel for Respondent :- C.S.C.
Hon'ble Abdul Moin,J.
1.

Heard learned counsel for the petitioner and learned Standing counsel appearing on behalf of State-respondent(s).
2. Under challenge is the order dated 24.09.2018, a copy of which is annexure 1 to the petition,
passed by the respondent No.2 whereby, while deciding the representation of the petitioner, the respondents have refused to take back the petitioner on the contractual post on which he was working and also terminated his contractual service w.e.f. 30.06.2018.
3.

Bereft of unnecessary details, the facts set forth by learned counsel for the petitioner are that the petitioner was working on contractual basis on the post of Welder under the respondent No.2 since the year 2008.
The contract used to be extended for 5 years at a stretch of time.
The last extension of the contract of the petitioner was done for the period from 23.08.2014 till 22.08.2019.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Even before the said contract could come to an end, on account of a dispute between the petitioner and his wife, an F.I.R. under Sections 498A, 323, 506 I.P.C. and Sections 3/4 of the Dowry Prohibition Act was registered at Police Station Bazar Khala, District Lucknow resulting in Case Crime No.57 of 2013.
He was thereafter incarcerated in jail.
Subsequently, he was granted bail by the High Court and reported for duty but was not permitted to join.
Thereafter, the petitioner has been convicted by the learned trial court for the aforesaid offences.

5. The competent authority, by means of the order impugned dated 24.09.2018, has terminated the contractual service of the petitioner w.e.f. 30.06.2018 itself on the ground of pendency of a criminal case against the petitioner, the petitioner having been convicted of the said offences and the petitioner having failed to indicate about his involvement in the said criminal case to the competent authority.

6. The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner is that upon a Criminal Revision No.641 of 2018 in Re: Suprabhat Banerjee vs. State of U.P. and Anr. being filed by the petitioner against the order of Criminal Appeal No.38 of 2018 filed by the petitioner against the judgment and order dated 19.01.2018 per which his appeal had been dismissed against his conviction, this Court has allowed the criminal revision by means of the judgment and order dated 15.03.2024 and the conviction and sentence of the petitioner, as imposed by the learned trial court, has also been set aside.
7.

entities.text: Suprabhat Banerjee vs. State of U.P. and Anr
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The contention of learned counsel for the petitioner is that once the conviction in the said criminal case has already been set aside by this Court, as such, the respondent No.2 be directed to consider the claim of the petitioner for being engaged on contractual basis, as the said conviction is no longer in force rather it has been set aside by this Court which was the primary ground which has prevailed upon the respondent No.2 while terminating the contractual service of the petitioner.

8. On the other hand, learned Standing counsel counsel has supported the order impugned on the ground of the petitioner having been convicted and the petitioner, after having been granted bail by this Court, having failed to indicate the aforesaid fact to the competent authority.

9. Having heard the learned counsels for the parties and perused the record, it emerges that the contractual service of the petitioner, which had been renewed from time to time since the year 2008,
the last renewal being up to 22.08.2019, have been terminated w.e.f. 30.06.2018 and the representation filed against the said order by the petitioner has also been rejected by means of the order impugned dated 24.09.2018.
10.
A perusal of the said order would indicate that primarily, the respondent No.2 has considered the conviction of the petitioner in Case Crime No.57 of 2013.
The said conviction has already been set aside by this Court vide judgment and order dated 15.03.2024.

Thus, it is apparent that the primary consideration which has prevailed on the respondent No.2, while terminating the contractual service of the petitioner and also while ending the contractual service of the petitioner vide order impugned dated 24.09.2018, is no longer in force.
The order impugned being prior to the conviction order of the petitioner having been set aside, it cannot be said that there is any infirmity in the said order.

sentences.text: However, considering the discussion as made above, the writ petition is disposed of with a direction to the respondent No.2 to consider the claim of the petitioner for being engaged on contractual basis on any suitable post in accordance with law and the relevant rules.
Let such consideration be done within a period of four weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this order.

12. It has been informed at Bar that the Airport premises are now being run by a private company,
as such, it is provided that it is only in case the respondent No.2 is at the helm of affairs that the consideration for the petitioner's claim would be done and in case the airport services or the place where the contractual services of the petitioner were available later have been passed on to a third party then obviously no such consideration would be made.
Order Date :- 5.12.2024/
